title: Nursing Home Abuse Linked to Corporate Profit Manipulation
discussion_signal: The post links related-party transactions and vertical integration to hidden nursing-home profits, financial opacity, staffing concerns, and public reimbursement. It translates the NBER tunneling result into an accountability question: can regulators and families see where facility revenue goes when operating entities transact with related real-estate, management, staffing, or vendor companies?
linked_research_question: How do related-party transactions, ownership structure, reported profits, staffing, public reimbursement, and resident outcomes connect, and which disclosure or payment rules can expose harmful tunneling without treating all integration as misconduct?
limits: The post is an advocacy-leaning translation and may overstate or simplify the underlying study
The discussion is not a regulatory finding or causal resident-outcome estimate
The linked research concerns a specific nursing-home setting and does not establish that every related-party transaction is harmful
